title: Hunters
summary: Mortals who hunt the Kindred: lonely, varied, and driven.

claims.text: Hunters are mortals who hunt vampires; their faces, methods and motives differ, but all seek the destruction of the Kindred.
A hunter knows the vampire only from real encounters, clouded by myth and legend.
Most hunters cannot know how widely the Kindred infest the world, only that something preys on their own home.
The mood is desperate determination.

title: Alone in the Crowd
summary: Why a hunter can expect no thanks and little help.

claims.text: No one hands out medals for killing vampires; even a trusted friend may see the same horror and deny it.
The higher a hunter appeals, the likelier it is to reach someone under vampire influence.
Stockpiling weapons or searching the wrong things online puts a hunter on watch lists, and burning a haven can bring charges of arson or murder.

title: The Big Leagues
summary: The organised hunter societies, seen from the street.

claims.text: Larger, organised hunter groups exist, but a lone hunter may find them bound up in their own protocols.
The Arcanum recruits only those with the right skills and temperament.
The Society of Leopold sends eager amateurs where it lacks the means to go, and prays for any who fall.
Project Twilight agents see civilian hunters as a threat to long operations.

title: The Kindred as Hunters See Them
summary: What a street hunter makes of vampire society.

claims.text: Vampires play at society with politics and sides, and loners are rare but strong.
One side keeps rules about being too obvious and answers to a Prince in each city, meeting in a council.
Its rules cover how much blood may be taken and how many deaths a neighbourhood can bear.
That side would often rather bargain with a hunter than be dragged into the light.
The other side worships its condition like a religion.

title: The Inquisition
summary: The Society of Leopold: the Church's crusaders against the Devil's children.

claims.text: No mortals frighten the Kindred more than the Inquisition.
Its theme is the modern crusader, with the whole world as Holy Land and the Devil as the Enemy.
Its four official sub-orders are the Condotierri, Gladius Dei, the Office of the Censor and the Order of Saint Joan; other groups count only as sects.
All its orders aim to deliver humanity from supernatural evil, though their methods differ and even clash.

title: The Arcanum
summary: A scholarly society that studies the supernatural.

claims.text: The Arcanum's charge is knowledge of the otherworldly, and its mandate is knowledge, not war.
Its theme is reckless exploration: members keep going where they know less than they should.
Chapter Houses support Lodges, one for a small House and up to five for a large one.
Lodges investigate reports of vampires, demons, werewolves and ghosts by interviewing witnesses and scouting.
The FBI's Special Affairs Division once hunted monsters with near freedom, and senior figures overlooked its orders for silver bullets and stakes.
Paperwork disguises the work: a raid on a werewolf compound is filed as a strike on terrorists with attack dogs, and silver rounds as Code Five.

title: Numina
summary: The gifts of psychics and hedge magicians.

claims.text: Psychics perceive hidden forces through extrasensory perception and can work on them with their minds.
Some are simply born with talents like telepathy, telekinesis or clairvoyance.
Telekinesis is rated by weight, from one pound at the first level to a thousand pounds at the fifth.

title: Hedge Magic
summary: Folk sorcery of paths and rituals.

claims.text: A hedge magician must hold a world view at odds with modern thinking: a working curse means unlucky thirteens, spilled salt and black cats matter too.

title: True Faith
summary: Divine favour that shields the faithful from the night.

claims.text: True Faith joins deep trust in the divine with divine favour, and only a blessed few have it.
The Faithful can repel vampires and ghosts with a holy symbol or prayer: spend Willpower and roll True Faith against the creature's permanent Willpower; each success is a turn it must flee.
Against a power that targets the Faithful directly and needs a roll, Faith is rolled at difficulty 7 and its successes subtract from the power's.
It gives no protection against passive or indirect uses of powers.

title: Hunters and Lupines
summary: When hunters cross paths with werewolves.

claims.text: A hunt may stray into werewolf lands, or one threat may menace hunter and werewolf alike.
As allies Lupines are dangerous; as enemies, deadly.
